sections.heading: Rate gap
sections.text: Absolute gap = |Japan rate − US rate| × 100 basis points when rates are in percent. Change = end gap − start gap. A negative change means narrowing. In this example, −3.00 → −2.50 percentage points is a smaller absolute gap: 300 → 250 bp.

sections.heading: Comparable inputs
sections.text: Both economies need comparable nominal instruments and qualified observations at both dates. Missing, stale, inaccessible or misaligned inputs make the comparison unavailable. Rates are shown in percent; currency settings do not change them.

sections.heading: Saved baseline
sections.text: This pair and date window has no matching saved baseline. Change across these dates is separate from change since saving. Expected paths and real rates use separate methods.
